title: Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty Old Master paintings organised by thresholds, viewpoints and the space bodies occupy.
introduction:
Vermeer's letter reader once appeared against a largely empty wall in widely reproduced photographs. Restoration revealed a large Cupid behind her. That change is a reminder that the image through which a painting becomes familiar may not show its present appearance, or even the surface its painter left.

Elsewhere in this Dresden selection, distance is deliberately constructed. A heavy table covering keeps a group beyond reach; curtains frame an approaching Madonna; a staircase measures the smallness of a child. Canaletto's canals offer several less intimate ways of entering an image. Comparing these devices is more useful than treating every work as an equally transparent window onto its subject.
visitNote: The selection concerns the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, not Dresden’s separate collection of later paintings. Check current loans and gallery information before visiting. The reproduction of Vermeer’s letter reader shows the painting before the restoration completed in 2021; the entry explains the change.

books.title: Dutch Paintings in The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Volumes I and II
books.author: Walter Liedtke
books.note: Walter Liedtke’s catalogue offers detailed accounts of Dutch painting, including Vermeer and Rembrandt. It supports further reading on their methods and subjects, although it catalogues the Metropolitan Museum’s works rather than Dresden’s.

works.title: Girl Reading a Letter at an Open Window
works.catalogueTitle: Girl Reading a Letter at an Open Window
works.credit: Johannes Vermeer. Girl Reading a Letter at an Open Window. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The girl reads beyond a foreground of fruit and patterned cloth. If the reproduction shows a bare wall behind her, it records an earlier condition: restoration brought a Cupid painting back into view. That figure changes both the room's balance and the letter's possible associations. Before interpreting the emptiness, check which state of the painting is being shown.

works.title: The Procuress
works.credit: Johannes Vermeer. The Procuress. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Hands converge above the richly patterned covering, making the exchange more concentrated than the crowded arrangement of faces might suggest. The heavy textile performs two jobs: it displays a closely worked surface and creates a barrier across the foreground. Vermeer brings the figures near while keeping their space on the other side of something substantial.

works.title: Acis and Galatea
works.credit: Claude Lorrain. Acis and Galatea. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/claude-lorrain/acis-and-galatea-1657
works.description: The mythological encounter occupies only a small part of Claude's landscape. Trees shelter the figures while water and bright distance extend beyond them. The setting therefore has its own progression from enclosure to openness, whether or not the viewer immediately identifies the lovers. The story receives a place within the landscape rather than commanding its entire scale.

works.title: Adoration of the Magi
works.credit: Adoration of the Magi. WikiArt; Nicolas Poussin. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Bending bodies and directed gestures gather attention around Mary and the child. Bright robes keep individual participants distinct inside the shared act of homage. Poussin's architecture provides a framework without turning the group into a rigid row. Devotion becomes legible through the repeated adjustment of one body towards another, rather than through a single isolated expression.

works.title: Entrance to the Grand Canal, Looking East
works.catalogueTitle: Entrance To The Grand Canal Looking East
works.credit: Canaletto. Entrance To The Grand Canal Looking East. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/canaletto/entrance-to-the-grand-canal-looking-east-1725
works.description: The water opens a broad viewing area in front of the buildings. Small boats cross it, giving the monumental architecture a scale tied to ordinary movement. Canaletto makes the canal available both as a prospect and as a working route. The vessels prevent the façades from becoming a collection of detached architectural elevations.

works.title: The Grand Canal towards the Rialto Bridge
works.catalogueTitle: Grand Canal: Looking North East toward the Rialto Bridge
works.credit: Canaletto. Grand Canal: Looking North East toward the Rialto Bridge. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/canaletto/grand-canal-looking-north-east-toward-the-rialto-bridge
works.description: The bend of the waterway brings façades into view at different angles. A single stretch of canal can therefore accommodate several architectural rhythms rather than one orderly recession. Boats occupy the intervals between the banks. Their changing positions help connect the carefully described buildings to a city that must be navigated as well as looked at.

works.title: The Grand Canal from Palazzo Balbi
works.catalogueTitle: Grand Canal: Looking from Palazzo Balbi
works.credit: Canaletto. Grand Canal: Looking from Palazzo Balbi. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/canaletto/grand-canal-looking-from-palazzo-balbi
works.description: Here the breadth of the canal competes with the buildings for attention. Relatively open water separates the long rows of façades, and the boats punctuate rather than fill it. Compared with the neighbouring canal views, the scene makes distance between the banks especially consequential. A changed viewpoint reorganises a familiar subject without requiring new landmarks.

works.title: Drunken Silenus
works.credit: Silenus Drunk. WikiArt; Anthony van Dyck. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The supporting figures give Silenus's weight a visible consequence. His heavy body leans into theirs, so mythology becomes a practical problem of balance within a crowded space. Warm flesh and red cloth bind the group together. Van Dyck allows bodily effort to carry the episode before any fuller explanation of its mythological company is required.

works.title: San Giacomo di Rialto
works.credit: Canaletto. San Giacomo de Rialto. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/canaletto/san-giacomo-de-rialto
works.description: Unlike the canal views, this picture organises movement around an open paved square. The church façade, with its conspicuous clock, supplies a stable centre while small figures cross the foreground. Canaletto makes the public space readable through the difference between permanent architecture and passing activity. The buildings define the square without exhausting what happens inside it.

works.title: The Martyrdom of Saint Catherine
works.credit: Lucas Cranach the Elder. The Martyrdom of St. Catherine. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/lucas-cranach-the-elder/the-martyrdom-of-st-catherine-1506
works.description: Rich clothing and crowded faces make Catherine's ordeal a public spectacle. The broken wheel and disturbed sky amplify the turbulence around her comparatively still kneeling figure. Cranach does not need to isolate the saint in empty space to distinguish her. Her posture stands apart precisely because so much surrounding activity competes for attention.

works.title: Saint John the Baptist
works.credit: Mateo Cerezo. Saint John thet Baptist. Image credit: Mateo Cerezo. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The staff and partial drapery establish the religious figure with little help from a setting. Cerezo turns the head towards a brighter area above, giving the standing body a direction of attention beyond its own outline. Darkness removes competing incident. The picture's action is largely an act of looking, made visible through the relation between face and light.

works.title: The Viola da Gamba Player
works.credit: Bernardo Strozzi. Gamba Player. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The instrument occupies enough space to establish an activity rather than functioning as a small identifying accessory. Above its curved body, the woman's gaze meets the viewer directly. Strozzi balances that encounter with the material presence of the instrument. Music is indicated through the sitter's relationship to an object, even though no sound can be supplied by the painting.

works.title: Heinrich, Count von Brühl
works.credit: Marcello Bacciarelli. Heinrich Graf Von Brühl. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/marcello-bacciarelli/heinrich-graf-von-bruhl-1753
works.description: Red and blue clothing declare the figure before the surrounding details are read. A table and architectural setting extend the formal presentation of rank. Bacciarelli distributes status across pose, costume and environment rather than leaving the face to explain it. The portrait shows how much a public likeness can communicate through things placed around a person.

works.title: Barbarina Campanini
works.credit: Rosalba Carriera. Portrait of Barbarina Campani. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Pale blue and white clothing keeps the portrait light against its subdued background. Jewellery and flowers introduce small points of distinction close to the face. Carriera's soft transitions do not erase the sitter; they establish her through delicate differences rather than hard boundaries. The work rewards attention to where one pale surface becomes another.

works.title: Man with a Hat Decorated with Pearls
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of a Man in the Hat Decorated with Pearls
works.credit: Portrait of a Man in the Hat Decorated with Pearls. WikiArt; Rembrandt van Rijn. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Selective illumination brings the face and decorated chest forward while leaving much of the hat unresolved in darkness. The supplied research classifies the painting among works by Rembrandt's followers, a qualification that should remain attached to its caption. A recognisable approach to light can circulate beyond one painter; resemblance of handling is not, by itself, an attribution.

works.title: Woman as a Vestal Virgin
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of a Woman as a Vestal Virgin
works.credit: Angelica Kauffman. Portrait of a Woman as a Vestal Virgin. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Pale drapery and a small vessel give the sitter an antique role without surrounding her with a fully narrated ancient event. Kauffman lets a portrait and a classical identity share the same figure. The turn towards the viewer preserves the directness of a likeness, while costume and gesture establish a second register in which the person is presented.

works.title: Presentation of the Virgin at the Temple
works.catalogueTitle: Presentation of the Virgin at the Temple
works.credit: Cima da Conegliano. Presentation of the Virgin at the Temple. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The staircase makes the child's ascent measurable. Its long open run separates the small climber from the waiting figure above and from onlookers below. Cima gives a modest bodily action ceremonial importance through architecture. The empty steps are active space: they make the distance visible and keep the ascent from disappearing among the surrounding people.

works.title: Rembrandt and Saskia in the Parable of the Prodigal Son
works.catalogueTitle: Self-Portrait with Saskia in the Parable of the Prodigal Son
works.credit: Rembrandt van Rijn. Self-Portrait with Saskia in the Parable of the Prodigal Son. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The raised glass and broad smile turn the pair into actors within a lively subject. Recognising Rembrandt and Saskia does not make the image an unmediated record of their home life. Costume, gesture and warm light establish a performance. The painting allows familiar likenesses to enter a story whose roles need not be identical to the sitters' lives.

works.title: The Sistine Madonna
works.credit: Raphael. The Sistine Madonna. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The parted curtains make the sacred group appear newly available to view. Below, the ledge and two small angels establish another boundary between the depicted space and the position outside it. Raphael brings Mary and the child forward while keeping that approach carefully framed. The familiar angels are part of this larger arrangement, not a separate decorative subject.

works.title: The Sleeping Venus
works.credit: Giorgione. The Sleeping Venus. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The body's long horizontal contour finds a counterpart in the rising and falling ground beyond it. Pale cloth separates the sleeper from the landscape without severing that connection. The extended arrangement makes repose a property of the whole picture, not merely a closed pair of eyes. Body and terrain establish their relation through shape rather than through a narrated event.

closingSections.title: Check the image as well as the caption
paragraphs: For Vermeer, compare an older reproduction with the museum's restored image. Elsewhere, retain attribution and dating qualifications when following these works into other sources. Display arrangements change; consult Dresden's current collection and visitor information before planning around an individual painting.
